scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: Fresh namespace held exactly 4 channels, 500 messages, and 3 profiles.
scenarioResults.note: Two public and two private channels each contained 125 seeded messages.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: Alice and Bob saw four channels; Mallory saw only public channels and both private read and subscription failed.
scenarioResults.note: The worktree-local JWT issuer is application glue for the anonymous local target; private keys were never retained.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: Bob independently read the settled row with Convex id, creation time, server sequence, author, and sentAt.
Bob's already-subscribed client observed Alice's unique committed message without product polling.
scenarioResults.note: Direct native client-session evidence; no browser automation was available.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: Two 25-row pages retained cursor values, had no duplicate ids, and stayed strictly sequence ordered across an intervening insert.
TTL filtering expired the visible typing actor, while durable inspection proved the row remained stored.
scenarioResults.note: Convex core supplied push but no native ephemeral typing primitive; the workaround is explicitly not counted as native ephemeral state.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: TTL filtering expired presence, while durable inspection proved the heartbeat row remained stored.
scenarioResults.note: Presence required application heartbeat, expiry, and cleanup glue.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: Messages committed while Bob was disconnected appeared after reconnect and all ids were unique.
Loaded history existed only in application JavaScript memory; no provider-owned cold-client persistent query cache was available.
scenarioResults.note: A copied array was not misreported as provider offline storage.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: Bob's unread count was 1 before and after reconnect, then 0 after the authoritative mark.
Promise.all from Alice and Bob preserved both rows with distinct adjacent server sequences and deterministic descending query order.
scenarioResults.note: Convex transactional mutations made the server sequence allocation simple.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: The established watch errored UNAUTHENTICATED, a fresh same-client private query was denied, and Alice's later committed message was not delivered.
scenarioResults.note: The original Stop candidate was a retained harness error caused by treating ConvexClient.setAuth(null) as logout. The raw delivery receipt's ConvexClient label is an erratum; executed source used ConvexReactClient.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: Membership removal errored Bob's watch, denied a fresh query, and blocked delivery of Alice's later private message.
scenarioResults.note: Prior values can remain in application-owned JavaScript variables; Convex supplied no persistent offline store to inspect or wipe.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: All five paths retained two warmups and seven raw samples plus median and nearest-rank p95.
scenarioResults.note: Representative read is a warm subscribed-client cache read; reconnect measures a fresh authenticated session. Results are local small-workload evidence, not hosted or scale evidence.

scenarioResults.authoritativeCheck: All namespace counts returned zero before the exact process stop; ports, matching processes, and exact runtime/CLI paths were absent afterward.
scenarioResults.note: Only the fresh local target and worktree-local runtime state were removed. Source, receipts, dependencies, and build output remain.
